findings.title: Unconstrained CIFAR-10 SOTA ceiling: ViT-H/14 (JFT-300M) at 99.5%
findings.finding: Unconstrained CIFAR-10 SOTA is 99.5% top-1 accuracy, held by ViT-H/14 pretrained on JFT-300M (Dosovitskiy et al. 2020); BiT-L (ResNet152x4, JFT-300M) achieves 99.37%; both confirmed by two independent leaderboards.
findings.evidence: ViT-H/14: 99.50% (CodeSOTA Oct-2020, wizwand.com leaderboard — sources agree within 0%); BiT-L: 99.37% (CodeSOTA Dec-2019); DeiT-B Distilled Open (Meta, Dec-2025): 99.10%; these models have 600M+ parameters and would require 1000+ ms CPU single-core inference.

findings.title: Small ResNet family on CIFAR-10: accuracy-FLOPs baseline from He et al. CVPR 2016
findings.finding: ResNet-20 (0.27M params, ~41M FLOPs) achieves 91.25% CIFAR-10; ResNet-32 (0.46M, ~69M FLOPs) achieves 92.49%; ResNet-56 (0.85M) achieves 93.03%; ResNet-110 (1.7M) achieves 93.39%.
findings.evidence: From He et al. CVPR 2016 Table 6, confirmed by Keras CIFAR-10 reproductions: ResNet-20 (20 layers, 0.27M params): 91.25%; ResNet-32 (0.46M): 92.49%; ResNet-56 (0.85M): 93.03%; ResNet-110 (1.7M): 93.39+/-0.16%. The CIFAR-adapted stem (3x3 conv stride-1 instead of 7x7 stride-2) is essential; wrong stem loses ~5pp.

findings.title: DAWNBench/myrtle.ai 9-layer ResNet: 94% accuracy but ~300-400M FLOPs, too slow for 1ms CPU
findings.finding: David Page's 9-layer ResNet (channels 64/128/256/512, ~6.6M params, ~300-400M FLOPs at 32x32) achieves 94% CIFAR-10 in 79s training on a V100; with TTA at 80 epochs achieves 96.1%; Keller Jordan (2024) reaches 94% in 3.29s / 95% in 10.4s / 96% in 46.3s on A100; however, inference is estimated 5-20ms on single x86 CPU core, disqualifying this architecture for the 1ms constraint.
findings.evidence: myrtle.ai/cifar10-fast: 94% accuracy, 24-epoch training in 79s on V100; 96.1% with TTA at 80 epochs; Keller Jordan arXiv 2024 (16 citations): 94% in 3.29s, 95% in 10.4s, 96% in 46.3s on NVIDIA A100 with derandomized horizontal-flip augmentation. Architecture: 9 conv layers, channel counts [64,128,256,512], producing ~300-400M FLOPs — inference time estimated 5-20ms single-core x86 (far above 1ms).

findings.title: ProxylessNAS: 97.92% CIFAR-10 with 5.7M params via hardware-aware NAS
findings.finding: ProxylessNAS achieves 2.08% test error (97.92% accuracy) on CIFAR-10 with 5.7M parameters, outperforming AmoebaNet-B with 6x fewer parameters; hardware-aware NAS directly targeting latency is the state-of-the-art approach for constrained deployment.
findings.evidence: ProxylessNAS CIFAR-10: 2.08% error = 97.92% accuracy, 5.7M params (Han Cai et al., ICLR 2019, 284 citations). FLOPs at 32x32 input not stated but estimated 100-300M — inference on single CPU core estimated 2-8ms, above 1ms budget. The mobile/CPU-specialized ProxylessNAS variant achieves 74.6% ImageNet at 6.1ms mobile GPU latency.

findings.title: CPU inference latency: TinyCNN 0.39ms single-thread on Pi 5 (ARM A76); MobileNetV3-Small 2.14ms on Pi 5 (4-thread)
findings.finding: TinyCNN (0.21 MB FP32 model, ~1-2M FLOPs at 32x32) runs in 0.392ms single-thread on ARM Cortex-A76 (Pi 5, 2.4GHz); MobileNetV3-Small (adapted for 32x32) runs 2.14ms on Pi 5 at 4 threads (~8ms single-thread); ResNet-18 takes 12.9ms on Pi 5 at 4 threads.
findings.evidence: Michel Jacob TechRxiv 2025: TinyCNN FP32 1-thread=0.392ms, 4-thread=0.114ms on Pi 5; MobileNet α=0.25 FP32 1-thread=0.202ms; MobileNetV3-Small 4-thread=2.14-2.17ms; ResNet-18 4-thread=12.9-14.1ms. INT8 is slower than FP32 on ARM SBC at batch=1 (TinyCNN INT8=0.397ms vs FP32=0.392ms) due to XNNPACK kernel maturity — quantize/dequantize overhead dominates arithmetic savings at this scale.

findings.title: Implied FLOPs budget for 1ms single-core CPU: ~3-5M FLOPs on ARM A76; ~20-50M FLOPs on x86 AVX2 INT8
findings.finding: Scaling from measured Pi 5 latency: ARM A76 2.4GHz single-core handles ~3-5M FLOPs in 1ms (extrapolated from TinyCNN at 0.39ms / ~2M FLOPs); modern x86 Core i7 at 3.6GHz with AVX2 INT8 is estimated 5-10x faster, giving ~20-50M FLOPs budget at 1ms — placing ResNet-20 (41M FLOPs) at the boundary for x86 INT8.
findings.evidence: Pi 5 ARM A76: TinyCNN ~2M FLOPs in 0.39ms → budget ~5M FLOPs at 1ms. Intel Core i7 AVX2 peak FP32: ~57 GFLOPS/core; at 20-30% efficiency: 11-17 MFLOPS; INT8 without VNNI: 2x = 22-34 MOPs; INT8 with VNNI (Ice Lake+): 4x = 44-68 MOPs. MobileNetV3-Small on Pi 4 (224x224) INT8: 23ms → confirms sub-1ms requires 32x32 input and highly optimized small models.

findings.title: MobileNet family on CIFAR-10: MobileNetV3-Small achieves ~93% accuracy; TripleNet-S achieves 90.25% at ~2.4ms on Pi 4
findings.finding: LCA+MobileNetV2 achieves 93.10% on CIFAR-10; LCA+ResNet-18 achieves 94.68%; TripleNet-S achieves 90.25% at 2.38ms per image on Raspberry Pi 4 (ARM Cortex-A72, 1.5GHz), which scales to approximately 0.25-0.48ms on modern x86 — comfortably under 1ms.
findings.evidence: Kanaparthi et al. 2026: LCA+MobileNetV2=93.10%, LCA+ResNet-18=94.68% on CIFAR-10. TripleNet arXiv 2204.00943: TripleNet-S accuracy=90.25%, inference=238ms per 100 images (=2.38ms/img) on Pi 4; MobileNetV2=384ms/100 (=3.85ms/img); GhostNet=252ms/100 (=2.52ms/img). All on Pi 4 ARM A72 1.5GHz; modern x86 AVX2 ~5-10x faster.

findings.title: Knowledge distillation on CIFAR-10: +0.18-0.30pp for ResNet pairs; KD may hurt very small models
findings.finding: Knowledge distillation from a ResNet-50 teacher to a ResNet-34 student yields +0.30pp gain (Feature-KD: 95.55% vs 95.25% baseline); gains are modest (+0.18-0.30pp) even for well-matched pairs; for tiny models (GhostNetV3-Small), all tested distillation strategies unexpectedly reduced accuracy below the 93.94% architectural baseline.
findings.evidence: Yasar 2026 (kd-capacity-gap): R50→R34 Feature-KD +0.30pp (95.55% vs 95.25%); R34→R18 Feature-KD +0.18pp; R50→R18 Logit-KD +0.21pp. Zager & Gardi 2025: GhostNetV3-Small baseline=93.94%; all distillation (standard KD, teacher assistants, teacher ensembles) reduced accuracy. Correcting the ResNet stem for 32x32 inputs gave >5pp improvement — larger than any KD gain.

findings.title: INT8 QAT retains 99.95%+ of CIFAR-10 FP32 accuracy; INT8 on ARM adds overhead not savings
findings.finding: INT8 QAT on CIFAR-10 NiN architecture: FP32=88.05%, INT8=88.01% (0.04pp loss — effectively zero); INT4 drops 0.35pp; INT2 drops 1.94pp; INT8 QAT is lossless in practice; however on ARM SBC at batch=1, INT8 is actually slower than FP32 due to runtime overhead — latency gains from INT8 require x86 VNNI or dedicated hardware.
findings.evidence: QGen arXiv 2404.11769: NiN CIFAR-10 FP32=88.05%, INT8=88.01% (Δ=-0.04pp), INT4=87.70% (Δ=-0.35pp), INT2=86.11% (Δ=-1.94pp). Pi 5 TinyCNN: INT8=0.397ms vs FP32=0.392ms (INT8 slower); Pi 5 MobileNet: INT8=0.419ms vs FP32=0.202ms (INT8 2x slower). Root cause: XNNPACK FP32 NEON kernels mature; INT8 quantize/dequantize overhead dominates at batch=1 small models.

findings.title: MCUNet hardware-aware NAS: 60-72% ImageNet at 27-521ms on STM32 MCU; implies ~3-15M FLOPs for 1ms equivalent
findings.finding: MCUNet (NeurIPS 2020) achieves first >70% ImageNet accuracy on commercial MCU (STM32) with 27-521ms latency using TinyEngine INT8; MCUNet-vww0 (VWW task, 27ms on STM32H743 at 216MHz) and AtomNet (AAAI 2025) further push to 64-73% ImageNet; these MCU measurements calibrate the FLOPs-to-latency relationship.
findings.evidence: MCUNet: TinyEngine on STM32H743 — mcunet-vww0: 27ms; mcunet-vww1: 51ms; mcunet-in0 (ImageNet): 28ms (48M FLOPs); mcunet-in4: 463ms (126M FLOPs, int8). AtomNet AAAI 2025: 64% ImageNet, 275ms on STM32F746 (80M FLOPs). STM32H743 @ 216MHz vs Intel Core i7 @ 3.6GHz: ~50-100x compute ratio → 50M FLOPs on MCU at 463ms ≈ 4.6-9.3ms on desktop x86 single-core — confirming ~10-50M FLOPs fits in 1ms on x86.

findings.title: MicroNet (ICCV 2021): 4-21M FLOPs achieve 46-62% ImageNet; CIFAR-10 equivalent expected ~90-93%
findings.finding: MicroNet (Li et al., ICCV 2021) achieves 46-62% ImageNet top-1 at 4-21M FLOPs using micro-factorized convolutions and Dynamic Shift-Max activations; at these FLOPs budgets on CIFAR-10 (10-class, 32x32), a well-designed MicroNet-style model is expected to achieve approximately 90-93% accuracy based on cross-dataset calibration.
findings.evidence: MicroNet-M0: 1.0M params, 4M MADDs, 46.6% ImageNet; MicroNet-M1: 1.8M, 6M MADDs, 51.4%; MicroNet-M2: 2.4M, 12M MADDs, 59.4%; MicroNet-M3: 2.6M, 21M MADDs, 62.5% ImageNet. Under 12M FLOPs, MicroNet outperforms MobileNetV3 by 9.6% on ImageNet. CIFAR-10 accuracy not directly measured; estimated 90-93% by analogy with ResNet-20 (91.25% at 41M FLOPs) and simpler task.

findings.title: LUT/Weightless neural networks: 84-88% CIFAR-10 on FPGA; no benefit for standard CPU inference
findings.finding: Weightless/LUT-based neural networks (BTHOWeN, LUTNet, H-WNN) achieve 84-88% CIFAR-10 accuracy on FPGA with dramatic energy/area savings vs DNNs; these approaches are FPGA-targeted and offer no latency advantage on standard CPU inference — not recommended for the CPU deployment scenario.
findings.evidence: H-WNN on FPGA: 84.62-88.23% CIFAR-10 accuracy (Table II, 4 variants); FINN-R BNN (1w1a): 84.19% CIFAR-10 on FPGA; BTHOWeN: 80% reduction in energy vs comparable DNN on FPGA. LUTNet: 91.1% CIFAR-10 on FPGA (binary weights). All results are FPGA-only. Truth Table Net achieves only 70% CIFAR-10 accuracy. No CPU latency measurements found for LUT-based inference.

findings.title: Once-for-All (OFA) NAS: 80% ImageNet under mobile constraints; no CIFAR-10-specific latency results
findings.finding: Once-for-All (Cai et al., ICLR 2020) achieves 80.0% ImageNet top-1 under mobile setting (<600M MACs) by training one supernet and specializing sub-networks per hardware; 1.5x faster than MobileNetV3 at same accuracy; technique is applicable to CIFAR-scale latency-constrained NAS but no CIFAR-10-specific sub-ms CPU results were published.
findings.evidence: OFA: 80.0% ImageNet <600M MACs (ICLR 2020); 4.0% accuracy over MobileNetV3 at comparable latency; ProxylessNAS (related): 97.92% CIFAR-10, 5.7M params (per arxiv 1812.00332). No published OFA result specifically targeting CIFAR-10 with <1ms CPU latency constraint found.

frontier_summary: At the hard constraint of ≤1ms single-core CPU inference (batch=1, int8, modern consumer x86 with AVX2), the realistic CIFAR-10 accuracy ceiling is approximately 91-93%: on x86 with AVX2 INT8 the effective FLOPs budget is ~20-50M ops/ms, placing ResNet-20 (41M FLOPs, 91.25%) at the boundary and ResNet-32 (69M FLOPs, 92.49%) just above it — the exact crossing point depends on whether VNNI is available; with training tricks (Cutout/CutMix augmentation, cyclic LR, label smoothing), architectures in the 30-50M FLOPs range can reach ~92-93%, with knowledge distillation adding a further +0.2-0.3pp. On ARM single-core (Pi-class), the 1ms budget allows only ~3-5M FLOPs, limiting accuracy to ~85-88%. The four biggest levers in order of impact are: (1) architecture sizing to target the 30-50M FLOPs regime matching the x86 int8 budget (not the channel-heavy 94%-accuracy DAWNBench model which needs ~300-400M FLOPs and 5-20ms CPU inference); (2) strong data augmentation — Cutout, CutMix, or AutoAugment give +1-2pp over baseline; (3) INT8 QAT (lossless: <0.05pp accuracy drop on CIFAR-10); and (4) knowledge distillation from a large pretrained teacher (+0.2-0.3pp, but architectural stem adaptation is a prerequisite and often more impactful than KD alone). The unconstrained SOTA ceiling is 99.5% (ViT-H/14 JFT-300M), leaving a ~6-8pp gap that is entirely attributable to the latency constraint.
